title: COBOL Exercises
description: Read each example in its lesson first. Predict the result, then check your answer. The notes explain the idea and one common mistake.

exercises.code:
identification division.
program-id. lesson.
data division.
working-storage section.

procedure division.
DISPLAY "Hello, Asha!"
stop run.
exercises.question: The procedure division holds steps. DISPLAY writes a value. STOP RUN ends the program. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: DISPLAY writes the quoted text. STOP RUN then ends the program. Compile these examples with -free because they use free-format source.

program-id. lesson.
data division.
working-storage section.
01 PENCILS PIC 9 VALUE 3.
procedure division.
DISPLAY PENCILS
stop run.
exercises.question: Working-storage holds data. PIC 9 describes one decimal digit. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The data description gives PENCILS the digit 3. DISPLAY reads it. PIC 9 holds one digit; choose a wider picture for bigger numbers.

exercises.code:
identification division.
program-id. lesson.
data division.
working-storage section.
01 PENCILS PIC 9 VALUE 3.
procedure division.
ADD 2 TO PENCILS
DISPLAY PENCILS
stop run.
exercises.question: ADD changes a numeric item by adding a value to it. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: ADD changes PENCILS from 3 to 5. Make sure the result fits the item picture.

exercises.code:
identification division.
program-id. lesson.
data division.
working-storage section.
01 ANSWER PIC 9.
procedure division.
COMPUTE ANSWER = 3 * 2
DISPLAY ANSWER
stop run.
exercises.question: COMPUTE assigns the result of a calculation. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: COMPUTE multiplies 3 by 2 and stores 6 in ANSWER. A field that is too small can lose digits.

exercises.code:
identification division.
program-id. lesson.
data division.
working-storage section.
01 SCORE PIC 9 VALUE 8.
procedure division.
IF SCORE >= 5
 DISPLAY "Pass"
ELSE
 DISPLAY "Try again"
END-IF
stop run.
exercises.question: IF checks a rule. END-IF marks where its branches finish. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The SCORE value 8 passes the test, selecting Pass. End the conditional with END-IF before unrelated steps.

exercises.code:
identification division.
program-id. lesson.
data division.
working-storage section.
01 LIGHT PIC X VALUE "G".
procedure division.
EVALUATE LIGHT
 WHEN "R" DISPLAY "Stop"
 WHEN "G" DISPLAY "Go"
 WHEN OTHER DISPLAY "Wait"
END-EVALUATE
stop run.
exercises.question: EVALUATE selects steps by matching a value. WHEN OTHER is a fallback. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The G value matches the second WHEN branch, which displays Go. Use a picture large enough for each label.

exercises.code:
identification division.
program-id. lesson.
data division.
working-storage section.
01 N PIC 9.
procedure division.
PERFORM VARYING N FROM 1 BY 1 UNTIL N > 3
 DISPLAY N
END-PERFORM
stop run.
exercises.question: PERFORM VARYING updates a counter and repeats until its stop rule is true. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: N starts at 1 and increases each pass. The loop stops when N reaches 4. Check that the counter changes toward the stopping rule.

exercises.code:
identification division.
program-id. lesson.
data division.
working-storage section.
01 SCORES.
 05 SCORE PIC 9 OCCURS 3 TIMES.
procedure division.
MOVE 4 TO SCORE(1)
MOVE 5 TO SCORE(2)
MOVE 8 TO SCORE(3)
DISPLAY SCORE(2)
stop run.
exercises.question: OCCURS makes repeated data items. Subscripts start at 1 in COBOL. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: Three MOVE steps fill the table. SCORE(2) reads its middle item, 5. A table subscript must stay within its declared count.

exercises.code:

program-id. lesson.
data division.
working-storage section.
01 STUDENT-NAME PIC X(4) VALUE "Asha".
procedure division.
DISPLAY STUDENT-NAME
stop run.
exercises.question: PIC X describes a character. A number in parentheses gives the field length. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The four-character field contains exactly Asha. Longer text needs a larger field or it will be cut short.

program-id. lesson.
data division.
working-storage section.

procedure division.
DISPLAY FUNCTION UPPER-CASE("asha")
stop run.
exercises.question: UPPER-CASE is a built-in function that makes letters uppercase. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: UPPER-CASE makes a new text result with capital letters. Call this with FUNCTION before the function name.

exercises.code:
identification division.
program-id. lesson.
data division.
working-storage section.
01 PET PIC X(3) VALUE "cat".
01 SIZE-NUM PIC 9.
procedure division.
COMPUTE SIZE-NUM = FUNCTION LENGTH(PET)
DISPLAY SIZE-NUM
stop run.
exercises.question: LENGTH gives the declared length of this text field, including any spaces. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: LENGTH measures the declared three-character size of PET. Field length includes padding spaces; it is not always the typed word length.

exercises.code:
identification division.
program-id. lesson.
procedure division.
PERFORM GREET
STOP RUN.
GREET.
DISPLAY "Hello again".
exercises.question: A paragraph labels a group of steps. PERFORM runs that paragraph and returns. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: PERFORM enters GREET and returns afterward. STOP RUN prevents later fall-through. STOP RUN before paragraph definitions prevents accidental fall-through at the end.
